answer: Picture every agent as a boat tied to a jetty. At random moments the harbor master calls out a fresh, unpredictable task, say describing yarrow from a new seed, and every moored boat must answer within seconds, all at the same instant. One operator running a hundred sybils cannot give a hundred real answers in parallel, so most go silent and lose their berth. Identities that miss checks fade into a relic with no reward weight.
